root_cause.text: In `netfilter/nf_tables` map catchall handling, the activation/deactivation code stopped after the first matching catchall element, so when both a live and a pending catchall existed during a transaction it failed to toggle all of them, leaving a dangling reference to map-backed element data that was later double-freed/dereferenced during abort cleanup.
root_cause.evidence: The patch removes the `break;` from both `nft_map_catchall_deactivate()` and `nft_map_catchall_activate()`, and the commit message says “we might have more than one catchall element: 1 live catchall element and 1 pending element” and that if the map is going away “its required to toggle all catchall elements and not just the first viable candidate,” otherwise triggering the `nft_data_release()` warning in `__nft_set_elem_destroy()` during `nf_tables_abort_release()`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix `nft_map_catchall_deactivate()` so it continues processing instead of stopping after the first catchall element.
intent_record.what: The diff removes a single `break;` statement from the loop inside `nft_map_catchall_deactivate()` after `nft_set_elem_change_active()` and `nft_setelem_data_deactivate()` are called.
intent_record.how: By removing the `break`, the function no longer exits the loop after processing the first matching element, so subsequent iterations can continue and potentially deactivate additional eligible catchall elements.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove an incorrect early break in `nft_map_catchall_activate()` to restore the intended control flow.
intent_record.what: The `break;` statement was removed from the `switch`/case block inside `nft_map_catchall_activate()`, so execution will no longer exit the case immediately after `nft_setelem_data_activate(ctx->net, set, catchall->elem);`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the code now continues past that point instead of terminating the case early, which changes control flow and may allow subsequent statements in the same `switch` case or fallthrough logic to run.

Fixing deactivation to continue processing addresses that issue.

The root cause is that catchall activation/deactivation stopped after the first matching element, leaving other live/pending catchalls untoggled and causing dangling references. Removing the incorrect early break in nft_map_catchall_activate() directly addresses that failure mode.

This early break stops nft_map_catchall_activate() after the first matching catchall element, preventing all relevant catchall elements from being activated and contributing to inconsistent state that can leave dangling references during transaction abort cleanup.

vuln_statements.explanation: This early break in the catchall handling loop stops nft_map_catchall_deactivate() or nft_map_catchall_activate() after the first matching element, so when both live and pending catchall entries exist during a transaction, the remaining one is not toggled and later abort cleanup can leave dangling map-backed element data that is double-freed or dereferenced.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct described in the root cause is not present here. The bug was that catchall activation/deactivation stopped after the first matching element, leaving other matching catchalls untouched. In this snippet, the relevant paths explicitly walk and handle map elements and catchalls: `nft_map_deactivate()` does `set->ops->walk(ctx, set, &iter);` and then `nft_map_catchall_deactivate(ctx, set);`, while `nft_map_catchall_deactivate()` iterates `list_for_each_entry(catchall, &set->catchall_list, list)` and deactivates active entries. The same pattern exists for activation in `nft_map_activate()` / `nft_map_catchall_activate()`. This shows the fix behavior is already present, not the buggy "stop after first matching catchall" logic. Therefore `has_bug` is false and `is_fixed` is true.
